balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

minorityInterest.title: Attributable vs minority-interest net profit
minorityInterest.content:
Net income (attributable) is the parent shareholders' share of profit -- the number the rest of this dashboard's EPS, margin and FCF charts use. Net profit incl. minority is the whole group's profit, before splitting off what belongs to non-controlling shareholders.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the Hisense-Hitachi HVAC joint venture, which generates the majority of group profit, is only ~49-51% owned by the parent. FY2025 group profit was ~RMB4.73bn against ~RMB3.19bn attributable -- roughly RMB1.5bn, or 32% of total profit, went to minority shareholders (mostly Hitachi and other JV partners). The DCF taxes this leakage explicitly rather than assuming the parent captures the JV's full economics.

What to watch:

  • The attributable share narrowing or widening as the JV's profit mix shifts
  • Any change in the parent's ownership stake in the HVAC JV
  • Minority interest on the balance sheet (MinorityInterests, ~RMB4.05bn at FY2025) moving in step with the income-statement split

tradingFinancialAssets.title: Trading financial assets
tradingFinancialAssets.content:
Trading financial assets are wealth-management products, structured deposits and other short-term treasury instruments held on the balance sheet, shown here against cash & equivalents for scale.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: this pile reached ~RMB19-21bn by FY2025/H1-2026 -- larger than operating cash and, combined with cash, larger than the H-share market capitalisation. The DCF's valuation bridge applies a 35% trapped-capital discount to these assets (net of the minority's claim) because the market does not appear to value related-party deposits and treasury products at face; some sit with Hisense Finance Co., a controlling-shareholder captive, which is a governance and accessibility question, not just a scale one.

What to watch:

  • The pile growing faster than operating cash flow (capital not being redeployed or returned)
  • Disclosure of counterparty concentration, especially related-party deposits
  • Any capital-return announcement that would test how accessible this balance really is

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Hisense Home Appliances Group Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: 2026-10-12: 35% trapped-capital discount (RMB-9,089m) on non-operating financial assets net of NCI, added to equity_bridge. Cause: balance-sheet discount (net financial assets > market cap), not peak earnings, WACC or growth. See valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_fix.
